title: Annotatio III §.VI: Recantation publicly confirms Paschasius’s conversion — and solemnly introduces dental laceration
pass_a_gloss: By which altogether then Paschasius Radbertus’s [teaching] on the Conversion of bread into Christ’s body is publicly confirmed, and that dental Laceration of Christ’s body — which seemed most absurd even to Paschasius himself — is solemnly introduced.
pass_b_english: That recantation publicly confirms Paschasius’s conversion of bread into Christ’s body.
It also solemnly introduces the dental laceration of Christ’s body — which Paschasius himself had found most absurd.
source_text: Quibus omninò tùm Paschasii Rhadeberti de Convers. panis in corpus Christi, publicè confirmatur, quàm absurdissima ipsi Paschasio visa Laceratio corporis Christi dentalis solenniter introducitur.

lemmas.latin: de Convers. panis in corpus Christi
lemmas.gloss: on the Conversion of bread into Christ’s body
